text:
Tara: Heads-up — saw a perf blip on canary during the multi-variant rollout. Latency spike + high token budget usage when compatset fallbacks kicked in.

Chris: ugh. which route/pool?

Tara: variant-routing -> pool-b; traffic shape: lots of short chats + occasional long continuations. Seems prefetch and KV warmup are colliding with continuous batching so batches get inflated.

Olga: can you paste the timeline/profile?

Tara: pasted below. Note the sawtooth in batch sizes when fallback starts, and KV cache miss rate jumps.

Tara: ```
# simplified pprof flame: serving_runtime.cpu
time  ms  cum
---
batch_form  12ms  (spike)
build_kv_prefetch  28ms  (concurrent)
kernel_select  3ms
decode  35ms
--
KV_miss_rate: 0.32 -> 0.71 after compat fallback
avg_batch_tokens: 48 -> 120 (during spike)
requests_dropped_for_token_budget: +12/min
```

Mike: Interesting that kernel_select is stable. My guess: the queue policy is allowing prefetch requests (for warmup) to join the same batch window as user requests, and the token budget threshold triggers a permissive merge. When a fallback variant joins, its sequence-length distribution differs -> larger per-request tokens -> token budget overshoot.

Chris: so we need 2 levers: tighten merge criteria for prefetch / warmup traffic, and reduce continuous batch window when compatset pressure detected.

Olga: +1. Also instrument an early-exit when KV warmup concurrency > X. Right now warmups spawn N prefetch requests per candidate variant. If routing fans out 3 variants, that's 3x warmup which floods the coalescer.

Tara: I tried a quick repro on dev cluster: config changes applied via runtime flags below. Results were promising (lower tokens, lower latency tail).

Tara: ```json
{
  "batch_window_ms": 6,
  "max_merge_prefetch": 0,
  "token_budget_target": 90,
  "compat_prefetch_limit": 1
}
```

Tara: after change: avg_batch_tokens 60 -> 44, p95 latency -18%, KV_miss_rate peak down to 0.42.

Mike: Nice. What about quality regressions? any difference in returned tokens for Llama-variant vs fallback?

Tara: No quality diffs in sample set (ran the existing evals). Main side-effect: slightly higher throughput cost because fewer prefetches -> a few cold starts, but still within budget.

Chris: I'd prefer a heuristic: when compatset size > 1 and fallback rate > 5%, set batch_window_ms to 4 and max_merge_prefetch to 0 for that pool. This avoids global changes.

Olga: Also add a soft token_budget_headroom factor: target * 0.85 when fanout > 2. That buys us headroom before splintering batches.

Tara: + propose to add an admission check into the coalescer: reject joining the batch if (is_prefetch && batch_tokens_remaining < estimated_prefetch_cost). That prevents prefetch from causing overshoot.

Mike: can we get the scheduler to mark prefetch requests with lower priority and a separate backpressure counter? Then routing can back off variant warmups if pending_prefetch > threshold.

Chris: yep. Implementation plan: 1) metric flags (fanout, pending_prefetch, kv_miss). 2) local heuristic in coalescer (admit logic). 3) per-pool dynamic batch_window. 4) rollout on canary then blue/green.

Tara: I opened a draft PR with the admit check + config flags: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/8321 (will flesh tests).

Olga: can you add a small smoke test that simulates 3-variant fanout with mixed seq-lens? We should assert token_budget not exceeded and p95 latency < target.

Tara: will do.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for runtime cluster "pool-b-canary". ID: deploy-9843.

Mike: After PR is merged, also add tracing tags for compatset_id and prefetch_origin so we can correlate in the console dashboard.

Chris: agree. Also add a cost metric for prefetch_count and prefetch_success_rate (useful for Optimize feature later).

Olga: one more thing — kernel selection: since we're shrinking batch windows on detected pressure, we should ensure the kernel fallback path for small batches remains fast. Add microbench for 1-8 token batches on both quantized and non-quantized paths.

Tara: noted. I ran a microbench locally — small batches hit 0.8x decode throughput compared to large stable batches, but still < p95 thresholds. I'll add the microbench results to the PR.

Chris: ok let's land admit-check behind a runtime flag, roll on pool-b canary, watch metrics for 30m, then decide. Thanks team :) :thumbsup:

Tara: thanks — pushing tests + bench results shortly.

Mike: ping me once canary metrics start flowing, I'll join the watch.

Tara: will do.
